title: New Asperterol from the coral associated fungus Aspergillus terreus, which protects against UVB induced damage through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and barrier repair mechanisms.
authors: Tang, Guangming; Zhang, Yi; Qian, Zhong-Ji
journal: Journal of photochemistry and photobiology. B, Biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究海洋真菌来源化合物B-1对UVB诱导皮肤光损伤的保护机制，核心为抗氧化、抗炎和屏障修复，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation, a primary cause of skin photoaging, triggers oxidative stress, inflammation, barrier dysfunction, and apoptosis in keratinocytes. New marine-derived benzaldehyde compound B-1 (Asperterrol), isolated from the coral-associated fungus Aspergillus terreus C23-3, has been demonstrated to have multifaceted protective effects against UVB-induced photoaging in HaCaT keratinocytes. This study revealed that B-1 restores cell viability at concentrations ranging from 2.5 to 10 muM and significantly reduces ROS overproduction, particularly at 10 muM, comparable to untreated controls. Mechanistically, B-1 activated the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway by promoting Nrf2 nuclear translocation and enhancing superoxide dismutase (SOD-1) expression, as evidenced by molecular docking showing stable hydrogen bonding with nuclear factor (Nrf2) residues (Val606 and Ile559). Concurrently, B-1 suppressed ultraviolet radiation B (UVB)-triggered inflammation via dose-dependent inhibition of inhibitor of NF-kB alpha (IkappaBalpha) phosphorylation and NF-kappaB/MAPK signaling, reducing cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and IL-1beta levels. Notably, B-1 upregulated skin barrier proteins Filaggrin and Involucrin, thereby counteracting UVB-induced barrier dysfunction. Furthermore, B-1 further mitigated apoptosis by normalizing the Bcl-2/Bax ratio and suppressing caspase-3 and caspase-9 activation while enhancing early-stage cell migration. These findings underscore the potential of B-1 as a promising multitarget agent against UVB-driven skin damage, bridging marine fungal resources to dermatological innovation.
abstract_zh: 中波紫外线（UVB）辐射是皮肤光老化的主要原因，可引发角质形成细胞中的氧化应激、炎症、屏障功能障碍和细胞凋亡。从珊瑚相关真菌 *Aspergillus terreus* C23-3 中分离出的新型海洋来源苯甲醛化合物 B-1（Asperterrol），已被证明对 UVB 诱导的 HaCaT 角质形成细胞光老化具有多方面的保护作用。本研究揭示，B-1 在 2.5 至 10 μM 浓度范围内恢复细胞活力，并显著减少活性氧（ROS）的过度产生，尤其在 10 μM 时效果显著，与未处理对照组相当。机制上，B-1 通过促进 Nrf2 核转位和增强超氧化物歧化酶（SOD-1）表达来激活 Nrf2/HO-1 抗氧化通路，分子对接显示其与核因子（Nrf2）残基（Val606 和 Ile559）形成稳定氢键。同时，B-1 通过剂量依赖性抑制 NF-κB 抑制剂 α（IκBα）磷酸化及 NF-κB/MAPK 信号通路，降低环氧合酶-2（COX-2）、诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）、白细胞介素-6（IL-6）和 IL-1β 水平，从而抑制 UVB 触发的炎症反应。值得注意的是，B-1 上调皮肤屏障蛋白 Filaggrin 和 Involucrin，从而对抗 UVB 诱导的屏障功能障碍。此外，B-1 通过恢复 Bcl-2/Bax 比值、抑制 caspase-3 和 caspase-9 激活，并增强早期细胞迁移，进一步减轻细胞凋亡。这些发现强调了 B-1 作为针对 UVB 驱动的皮肤损伤的多靶点药物的潜力，将海洋真菌资源与皮肤病学创新联系起来。
